prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: parsing the WWW-Authenticate header used naive/substring matching that could misfire on comma-containing or lookalike text inside quoted auth-param values (e.g. a quoted realm/resource_metadata value containing a comma or the substring of another param name). Both add a quote-aware, escape-aware comma-splitter to tokenize the header into proper auth-param segments before extracting fields. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: parsing the WWW-Authenticate header used naive/substring matching that could misfire on comma-containing or lookalike text inside quoted auth-param values (e.g. a quoted realm/resource_metadata value containing a comma or the substring of another param name). Both add a quote-aware, escape-aware comma-splitter to tokenize the header into proper auth-param segments before extracting fields. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the *entire* raw header (not just the text after the first space) and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly scans segments for a scheme token (e.g. 'Bearer') before collecting its params. That means it correctly isolates the Bearer challenge even when the header contains multiple challenges/schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one scheme's auth-params, which would incorrectly fold a second scheme's name and params into the first scheme's parameter list if more than one challenge is present in the header.

members.title: fix(server): don't raise when tool_use is not followed by tool_result
members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the exact same branch of validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that handles an assistant tool_use with no following tool_result — but they resolve it in opposite, mutually exclusive ways. #2962 changes the guard to `has_tool_results and has_previous_tool_use and previous_content`, so when there are no tool_results at all, the id-matching block is skipped entirely and no error is raised. Its regression test cites SEP-1577 to argue the spec has no requirement that a tool_use must be followed by a tool_result, so raising here was itself the bug. #3053 keeps the original (still-raising) behavior and instead adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` before the id-match check, just to give a clearer message — i.e. it assumes raising in this case is correct and only improves the error text. Merging both would be incoherent: #3053's added raise is unreachable if #2962 lands first, and #2962's fix is negated if #3053 lands first. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: 3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the *entire* raw header (not just the text after the first space) and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly scans segments for a scheme token (e.g. 'Bearer') before collecting its params. That means it correctly isolates the Bearer challenge even when the header contains multiple challenges/schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="y"'). 3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead locates only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one scheme's auth-params, which would incorrectly fold a second scheme's name and params into the first scheme's parameter list if more than one challenge is present in the header.
